evidence: the-status-page-is-refused-off-loopback: manifests/nginx_frontend.pp:254-260 puts location /nginx_status on the monitoring server with location_allow ['127.0.0.1'] and location_deny ['all']; the probe sends the request to the node's enp0s8 address, so the source is not 127.0.0.1 and 403 is the expected result. The mismatch changes only the address to 127.0.0.1, the one allowed source, which must give 200 and so must fail the expect

the-monitoring-server-answers: line 222 builds the name <trusted hostname>.monitoring.<domain>, which is monitoring.p8test.example.com under the fixture's domain; line 265 pins that name to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts (probed with getent); lines 241-248 return 200 'Hello World!\n' with default_type text/plain (nginx turns the \n into a newline); lines 254-260 enable stub_status for 127.0.0.1, whose first line is 'Active connections: N '. The expect matches all of this

the-nginx-status-check-reports: lines 270-276 install /opt/puppet-infrastructure/bin/check_nginx_status.py as root:root 0755 (localdir is lookup filesystem::localdir). The baseline template reads http://<fqdn_monitoring_server>/nginx_status; its defaults are warn 50 and crit 100, so it exits 0 on an idle node. Active_Connections is at least 1 (the check's own request), so -m 0 exceeds the warning threshold (exit 1) and -M 0 exceeds the critical one (exit 2). The probe and expect match the template's logic

purpose covered: The purpose matches the baseline header (domain servers through nginx_frontend_domain, the certificate bundle through ssl_nginx_domain, the default server) plus the monitoring server and Nagios check of lines 208-277. The checks exercise each part on the applied node: HTTP-to-HTTPS 301 on the domain and www, keeping the path; the HTTPS proxy to a live backend, with the certificate verified against the bundle's issuer under both names and rejected under other.example.com; TLS 1.3 accepted and TLS 1.2 refused; 404 over HTTP and HTTPS for an unknown name (with a mismatch on the held name), which also shows that the package's default site was removed (nginx_default_removal), since otherwise it would conflict with or pre-empt default_server; the monitoring server through its /etc/hosts pin, the Hello World text/plain answer and the stub status from loopback; 403 off loopback (added in correction 1); and the Nagios check's OK/WARNING/CRITICAL exits. The uncovered rows are honest: parameter variants (redirect_default, no default or monitoring server, no SSL, Let's Encrypt, ip_whitelist, pass-throughs) need other fixtures, and one set holds one fixture; the RedHat private-key directory (lines 87-99) needs rhel9
